adjudicated.ruling: The j-form against this edition's i-form, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. This edition prints i because the books it edits do: the 1962 typical edition sets Iesu, Ioánnem, iube and maiestátis throughout, and so does the Mszał Rzymski of the Tyniec Benedictines (Pallottinum, Poznań 1963), which is the book a Polish reader is most likely to hold. The mid-century hand missals print j; neither spelling is a different word, and the apparatus records theirs.

No comma inside the string of appositions naming the Son, with handmissal-eo and with the corpus rulings at ordinarium.confiteor w064 and ordinarium.aufer-a-nobis w018: Jesus Christus Fílius tuus Dóminus noster is one unbroken title, and cutting it once would require cutting it twice.
No comma before the second apposition, with handmissal-eo — parallel to w031 in the same title.

No comma before the trailing Deus, with DO: Deus is in apposition to the subject Qui, the same construction the corpus leaves unbroken at w031, and a comma here would read as though a new address began.
